definitions.explanation: The lowest temperature at which a liquid gives off enough vapor to catch fire when a flame or spark is brought near it.

examples.japanese: ⟦ガソリン→ガソリン：01346_gasorin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{引火点|いんかてん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{低|ひく}い→低い：02947_hikui⟧。
examples.english: Gasoline has a low flash point.

examples.japanese: {引火点|いんかてん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦{油|あぶら}→油：01693_abura⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: We use an oil with a high flash point.

examples.japanese: ⟦{灯油|とうゆ}→灯油：04071_touyu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{引火点|いんかてん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{四十度|よんじゅうど}⟦{以上|いじょう}→以上：01308_ijou⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦ガソリン→ガソリン：01346_gasorin⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{安全|あんぜん}→安全：01131_anzen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{扱|あつか}える→扱う：01862_atsukau⟧。
examples.english: Kerosene has a flash point of over forty degrees, so it is safer to handle than gasoline.

notes:
Composed of {引火|いんか} (catching fire from a nearby flame) + ⟦{点|てん}→点：01553_ten⟧ (point).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {発火点|はっかてん}: ignition point — the temperature at which a substance ignites by itself, with no flame; always higher than the flash point
- ⟦{沸点|ふってん}→沸点：25307_futten⟧: boiling point
